questions.prompt: Idealism, as defined at the outset, holds that:
choices: A Only material atoms exist mind-independently.
B There isn’t a mind-independent world—everything depends on mind.
C Ethics is impossible.
D Time is unreal but space is fully mind-independent.
A The sun inside the earth.
B Sources of universal/necessary structure toward the subject/mind.
C All science to astrology.
D Empiricism to pure skepticism only.

questions.prompt: Against treating “7+5=12” as merely analytic, Kant insists:
choices: A Arithmetic is only verbal tautology with no construction.
B You must construct/combine the units—not given just by analyzing concepts.
C Math is empirical counting of pebbles only.
D Arithmetic is synthetic a posteriori solely.

questions.prompt: For Kant, a priori concepts/laws of understanding are:
choices: A Optional habits.
B Necessary conditions for the possibility of experience of objects as we experience them.
C Only social conventions with no epistemic role.
D Descriptions of noumena directly.

questions.prompt: Space and time, in the Kantian picture, are:
choices: A Properties of things-in-themselves known by telescopes.
B Forms of sensibility—everything we perceive is in space and/or time.
C Invented in the 19th century.
D Irrelevant to experience.
